Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

not lift a finger phrase

also sit on one’s hands, sit on your hands, do nothing, twiddle one’s thumbs, sit idle

classical

Liv. 7.13.7 (Lewis & Short), s.v. comprimō
Traupman 99: compressīs manibus sedēre, sit on one’s hands

compressīs manibus sedēre

ablative absolute with sedeō

sit with folded hands, sit idle

Lewis & Short: “with the hands folded, i.e. to be unemployed, at leisure” (a proverb).

Other words

  • nē digitum quidem porrigere — not stir a finger

    porrigō with digitum; nē … quidem round the noun · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. digitus: “not to stretch out a finger … not to give one’s self the least trouble”

  • pressīs manibus sedēre — not lift a finger

    also used · modern · Traupman 98; Traupman 315

    Traupman’s form on p. 98; on p. 99 he gives compressīs manibus, which is the phrase Lewis & Short cites from Livy. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

See also idle, slack off.

SourcesLewis & Short: comprimo · Lewis & Short: digitus · Lewis & Short: porrigo

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 98, 99, 315.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
